# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

public ActionResult processAction(final Action action)
{
    if (action instanceof Exit) {
        setIsExitSpecified(true);
        Success result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
        result.setAction(action);
        return result;
    } else if (action instanceof Undo) {
        getState().undo();
        Success result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
        result.setAction(action);
        return result;
    } else if (action instanceof Move) {
        Move moveAction = (Move) action;
        Position currentPosition = getState().getPlayerPositionById(action.getInitiator());
        Position nextPosition = moveAction.nextPosition(currentPosition);
        Entity entity = getState().getEntity(nextPosition);
        if (entity instanceof Empty) {
            getState().move(currentPosition, nextPosition);
            Success result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
            result.setAction(action);
            return result;
        } else if (entity instanceof Box) {
            Box box = (Box) entity;
            if (box.getPlayerId() == action.getInitiator()) {
                Position pushTarget = moveAction.nextPosition(nextPosition);
                Entity targetEntity = getState().getEntity(pushTarget);
                if (targetEntity instanceof Empty) {
                    getState().move(nextPosition, pushTarget);
                    getState().move(currentPosition, nextPosition);
                    getState().checkpoint();
                    Success result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createSuccess();
                    result.setAction(action);
                    return result;
                } else {
                    Failed result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
                    result.setAction(action);
                    result.setReason("Cannot push box into occupied space");
                    return result;
                }
            } else {
                Failed result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
                result.setAction(action);
                result.setReason("Move blocked");
                return result;
            }
        } else {
            Failed result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
            result.setAction(action);
            result.setReason("Move blocked");
            return result;
        }
    } else if (action instanceof InvalidInput) {
        InvalidInput invalidInput = (InvalidInput) action;
        Failed result = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createFailed();
        result.setAction(action);
        result.setReason(invalidInput.getMessage());
        return result;
    }
    // Should not reach here
    throw new UnsupportedOperationException();

1. Compute context information
  1.1 Navigate the Ecore model to find related classes
  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. A method is unimplemented if its body contains `// TODO: Please complete this Java method based on the docstring`.
3. For every unimplemented method, 
  3.1 You must read the docstring of this method. The fragment between `<!-- begin-model-doc -->` and `<!-- end-model-doc -->` contains the method specification;
  3.2 Generate your code strictly according to the algorithm; Be aware of the EMF code style and APIs;
  3.3 You should not change the method signature;
  3.4 After generation, replace the current body with the one you generate;
  3.5 Keep and update the docstring by changing `@generated` to `@generated NOT`.
4. Check the import list. Add missing imports if needed.
5. Do not change other part.
6. Be aware of the method signatures, particularly, the input and output types, provided in the **Context**.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

  public void render(final GameState state)
```java
  {
```
    for (int y = 0; y < state.getBoardHeight(); y++) {
      String line = "";
      for (int x = 0; x < state.getBoardWidth(); x++) {
        Position pos = Pa22Factory.eINSTANCE.createPosition();
        pos.setX(x);
        pos.setY(y);
        Entity entity = state.getEntity(pos);
        if (entity instanceof Wall) {
          line += "#";
        } else if (entity instanceof Player) {
          line += (char)('A' + ((Player) entity).getId());
        } else if (entity instanceof Box) {
          line += (char)('a' + ((Box) entity).getPlayerId());
        } else if (state.getDestinations().contains(pos)) {
          line += "@";
        } else {
          line += ".";
        }
      }
      getOutputStream().println(line);
    }
    getOutputStream().println("Undos remaining: " + state.getUndoQuota());
  }

1. Compute context information
  1.1 Navigate the Ecore model to find related classes
  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. Read the error messages carefully.
3. Do your best to fix the errors locally without introducing new types, fields, and methods.
4. You should not remove faulty methods to eliminate compilation errors.
5. Do not change parts without errors.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

          state.move(currentPos, nextPos)

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

```text
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalSokobanGame::run
Summary: Runs the main game loop for the terminal-based Sokoban game. Renders the initial board, then repeatedly fetches actions from the input engine, processes them, prints messages, and renders the updated state until the game should stop.
Algorithm:
  render(state)
  while not shouldStop():
    action = inputEngine.fetchAction()
    result = processAction(action)
    renderingEngine.message(result.action.toString())
    render(state)
Related Features: state, inputEngine, renderingEngine, processAction, shouldStop, render
Related Classes: Action, ActionResult, GameState, InputEngine, RenderingEngine
Input: None
Output: None
Pre-condition: state has been initialized and contains at most two players
Post-condition: The game loop has terminated and the final state has been rendered

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).

  on the board).
```

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalInputEngine::fetchAction
Summary: Reads a single line of input from the terminal scanner and converts it to an Action object according to the command mapping.
Algorithm:
  Read a line from terminalScanner (trimmed, lowercased)
  If input is "exit": return new Exit(initiator=-1)
  If input is "w": return new Up(initiator=0)
  If input is "a": return new Left(initiator=0)
  If input is "s": return new Down(initiator=0)
  If input is "d": return new Right(initiator=0)
  If input is "k": return new Up(initiator=1)
  If input is "h": return new Left(initiator=1)
  If input is "j": return new Down(initiator=1)
  If input is "l": return new Right(initiator=1)
  If input is "r": return new Undo(initiator=0)
  If input is "u": return new Undo(initiator=1)
  Otherwise: return new InvalidInput(initiator=-1, message="Invalid input")
Related Features: terminalScanner
Related Classes: Action, Up, Down, Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput
Input: None
Output: Action - the parsed action
Pre-condition: terminalScanner is initialized and ready to read input
Post-condition: Returns an Action corresponding to the input command; returns InvalidInput for unrecognized commands

```text
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalInputEngine::fetchAction
Summary: Reads a single line of input from the terminal scanner and converts it to an Action object according to the command mapping.
Algorithm:
  Read a line from terminalScanner (trimmed, lowercased)
  If input is "exit": return new Exit(initiator=-1)
  If input is "w": return new Up(initiator=0)
  If input is "a": return new Left(initiator=0)
  If input is "s": return new Down(initiator=0)
  If input is "d": return new Right(initiator=0)
  If input is "k": return new Up(initiator=1)
  If input is "h": return new Left(initiator=1)
  If input is "j": return new Down(initiator=1)
  If input is "l": return new Right(initiator=1)
  If input is "r": return new Undo(initiator=0)
  If input is "u": return new Undo(initiator=1)
  Otherwise: return new InvalidInput(initiator=-1, message="Invalid input")
Related Features: terminalScanner
Related Classes: Action, Up, Down, Left, Right, Undo, Exit, InvalidInput
Input: None
Output: Action - the parsed action
Pre-condition: terminalScanner is initialized and ready to read input
Post-condition: Returns an Action corresponding to the input command; returns InvalidInput for unrecognized commands

# Requirement

```text
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
```

# Operation Specifications
TerminalRenderingEngine::render
Summary: Renders the current game state to the output stream as a text grid.
Algorithm:
  For y from 0 to state.boardHeight - 1:
      Initialize an empty line string
      For x from 0 to state.boardWidth - 1:
          Let pos = new Position(x, y)
          Let entity = state.getEntity(pos)
          If entity is Wall: Append '#'
          Else if entity is Player: Append upper-case letter corresponding to player ID (A for 0, B for 1, etc.)
          Else if entity is Box: Append lower-case letter corresponding to box.playerId (a for 0, b for 1, etc.)
          Else if pos is in state.destinations: Append '@'
          Else: Append '.'
      Print the line to outputStream
  Flush outputStream
Related Features: outputStream, state
Related Classes: GameState, Position, Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty
Input: state : GameState - the current game state to render
Output: void
Pre-condition: state is not null; outputStream is initialized
Post-condition: The game grid is printed to the output stream

# Operation Specifications
TerminalRenderingEngine::render
Summary: Renders the current game state to the output stream as a text grid.
Algorithm:
  For y from 0 to state.boardHeight - 1:
      Initialize an empty line string
      For x from 0 to state.boardWidth - 1:
          Let pos = new Position(x, y)
          Let entity = state.getEntity(pos)
          If entity is Wall: Append '#'
          Else if entity is Player: Append upper-case letter corresponding to player ID (A for 0, B for 1, etc.)
          Else if entity is Box: Append lower-case letter corresponding to box.playerId (a for 0, b for 1, etc.)
          Else if pos is in state.destinations: Append '@'
          Else: Append '.'
      Print the line to outputStream
  Flush outputStream
Related Features: outputStream, state
Related Classes: GameState, Position, Entity, Wall, Player, Box, Empty
Input: state : GameState - the current game state to render
Output: void
Pre-condition: state is not null; outputStream is initialized
Post-condition: The game grid is printed to the output stream

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

# Operation Specifications
GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Returns a list of all positions where players are located on the board.
Algorithm:
  Initialize an empty list of positions
  For each entry in entities map:
      If entity is Player:
          Add the entry's position to the list
  Return the list
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity, Player
Input: None
Output: List<Position> - list of all player positions
Pre-condition: entities is initialized
Post-condition: Returns list of positions where players are located; may be empty if no players exist

GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the game state using the transition/checkpoint history, consuming undo quota if finite and checkpoint exists.
Algorithm:
  if undoQuota == 0 then
    return
  if history.isEmpty() then
    return
  transition = history.pop()
  for each (from, to) in transition.reverse().moves do
    entity = entities.get(to)
    move(from, to)
  end for
  if undoQuota != -1 then
    undoQuota = undoQuota - 1
  end if
Related Features: history, undoQuota, entities
Related Classes: GameStateTransition, Position
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The game state is reverted to the previous checkpoint, and undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it is not -1 and a checkpoint was undone.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Checks if the game is won, i.e., every destination position is occupied by a Box.
Algorithm:
  for each position in destinations do
    entity = getEntity(position)
    if entity is not an instance of Box then
      return false
    end if
  end for
  return true
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Position, Box, Empty
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if all destinations are occupied by Boxes, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns true if every destination has a Box entity, false otherwise.
Summary: Determines whether the game loop should terminate, based on exit flag or win condition.
Algorithm:
  return isExitSpecified or state.isWin()
Related Features: isExitSpecified, state
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if exit is specified or the game is won, false otherwise
Pre-condition: state is not null
Post-condition: Returns true if isExitSpecified is true or state.isWin() returns true, otherwise false.

GameState::move
Summary: Moves an entity from one position to another, recording the transition.
Algorithm:
  Let entity = getEntity(from)
  Remove entity from from position in entities map
  Place entity at to position in entities map
  Add the move (from -> to) to currentTransition
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Position, Entity, GameStateTransition
Input: from : Position - current position; to : Position - destination position
Output: void
Pre-condition: from position has an entity; to position is empty; both positions are within board bounds
Post-condition: Entity is moved from 'from' to 'to'; the move is recorded in currentTransition

GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Records the current state as a checkpoint by pushing the current transition onto the history stack.
Algorithm:
  history.push(currentTransition)
  currentTransition = new GameStateTransition()
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The previous currentTransition is pushed onto history, and currentTransition is a new empty transition.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Finds the position of a player with the given ID.
Algorithm:
  for each position in getAllPlayerPositions() do
    entity = getEntity(position)
    if entity is Player and entity.id == id then
      return position
    end if
  end for
  return null
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: id : int - the player ID to search for
Output: Position - the position of the player with the given ID, or null if not found
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the position of the player with the specified ID if found, otherwise null.

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the entity at a specified position on the board.
Algorithm:
  Return entities.get(position)
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: position : Position - the position to query
Output: Entity - the entity at that position, or null if empty
Pre-condition: position is within board bounds (0 <= x < boardWidth, 0 <= y < boardHeight)
Post-condition: Returns the entity at the given position, or null if no entity exists there

# Operation Specifications
GameState::getAllPlayerPositions
Summary: Returns a list of all positions where players are located on the board.
Algorithm:
  Initialize an empty list of positions
  For each entry in entities map:
      If entity is Player:
          Add the entry's position to the list
  Return the list
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity, Player
Input: None
Output: List<Position> - list of all player positions
Pre-condition: entities is initialized
Post-condition: Returns list of positions where players are located; may be empty if no players exist

GameState::undo
Summary: Reverts the game state using the transition/checkpoint history, consuming undo quota if finite and checkpoint exists.
Algorithm:
  if undoQuota == 0 then
    return
  if history.isEmpty() then
    return
  transition = history.pop()
  for each (from, to) in transition.reverse().moves do
    entity = entities.get(to)
    move(from, to)
  end for
  if undoQuota != -1 then
    undoQuota = undoQuota - 1
  end if
Related Features: history, undoQuota, entities
Related Classes: GameStateTransition, Position
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The game state is reverted to the previous checkpoint, and undoQuota is decremented by 1 if it is not -1 and a checkpoint was undone.

GameState::isWin
Summary: Checks if the game is won, i.e., every destination position is occupied by a Box.
Algorithm:
  for each position in destinations do
    entity = getEntity(position)
    if entity is not an instance of Box then
      return false
    end if
  end for
  return true
Related Features: destinations, entities
Related Classes: Position, Box, Empty
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if all destinations are occupied by Boxes, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns true if every destination has a Box entity, false otherwise.
Summary: Determines whether the game loop should terminate, based on exit flag or win condition.
Algorithm:
  return isExitSpecified or state.isWin()
Related Features: isExitSpecified, state
Related Classes: GameState
Input: None
Output: boolean - true if exit is specified or the game is won, false otherwise
Pre-condition: state is not null
Post-condition: Returns true if isExitSpecified is true or state.isWin() returns true, otherwise false.

GameState::move
Summary: Moves an entity from one position to another, recording the transition.
Algorithm:
  Let entity = getEntity(from)
  Remove entity from from position in entities map
  Place entity at to position in entities map
  Add the move (from -> to) to currentTransition
Related Features: entities, currentTransition
Related Classes: Position, Entity, GameStateTransition
Input: from : Position - current position; to : Position - destination position
Output: void
Pre-condition: from position has an entity; to position is empty; both positions are within board bounds
Post-condition: Entity is moved from 'from' to 'to'; the move is recorded in currentTransition

GameState::checkpoint
Summary: Records the current state as a checkpoint by pushing the current transition onto the history stack.
Algorithm:
  history.push(currentTransition)
  currentTransition = new GameStateTransition()
Related Features: history, currentTransition
Related Classes: GameStateTransition
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: The previous currentTransition is pushed onto history, and currentTransition is a new empty transition.

GameState::getPlayerPositionById
Summary: Finds the position of a player with the given ID.
Algorithm:
  for each position in getAllPlayerPositions() do
    entity = getEntity(position)
    if entity is Player and entity.id == id then
      return position
    end if
  end for
  return null
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Player
Input: id : int - the player ID to search for
Output: Position - the position of the player with the given ID, or null if not found
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns the position of the player with the specified ID if found, otherwise null.

GameState::getEntity
Summary: Retrieves the entity at a specified position on the board.
Algorithm:
  Return entities.get(position)
Related Features: entities
Related Classes: Position, Entity
Input: position : Position - the position to query
Output: Entity - the entity at that position, or null if empty
Pre-condition: position is within board bounds (0 <= x < boardWidth, 0 <= y < boardHeight)
Post-condition: Returns the entity at the given position, or null if no entity exists there

# Requirement
```text
 ---                                                                        
  1. Overview                                                 
  This project implements a multi-player variant of the classic grid-based puzzle game called Sokoban. The core mechanic involves players moving around a closed-boundary map to push boxes to
  specific destinations. A unique feature of this variant is that it supports multiple players (up to 26), and each player can only push their designated boxes. The objective is to navigate the
  board and strategically place all boxes onto the designated targets. The game features customizable undo quotas, action validation, and a terminal-based text user interface (TUI).
  ---
  2. Functional Requirement
  2.1 Map parsing and validation
  The system manages 2D grid coordinates through the Position class. The game board is initialized via PA22Helper.parseGameMap, reading a text representation where:
  - The first line is undo limit.
  - # denotes walls.
  - . denotes empty spaces.
  - @ denotes destinations and the cell itself is an Empty entity.
  - Upper-case letters denote Player.
  - Lower-case letters denote Box that is only movable by the player with the corresponding upper-case letter (a ↔ A, b ↔ B, etc.).
  PA22Helper.parseGameMap also validates the map:
  - Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or a non-negative integer (values < -1 are invalid).
  - There must be at least one player in the map.
  - There must be no duplicated players (i.e., the same upper-case letter cannot appear more than once).
  - The number of destinations must equal the number of boxes.
  - Boxes must reference valid player IDs that exist in the map, and every player on the map must have corresponding boxes (i.e., the set of box-referenced player IDs equals the set of player IDs
  on the board).
  2.2 Game state and moves
  The dynamic game state is handled by GameState, which keeps track of entities and destinations. During Move actions (Up, Down, Left, Right), a player attempts to move to a nextPosition. A player
  can move into an Empty space or push a Box. A Box can only be pushed if it belongs to the initiating player (i.e., Box.getPlayerId() matches the Player's ID) and the space behind the box is
  empty. Movement is blocked by Wall, other players, or unpushable boxes.
  Each game action must return an ActionResult (Success or Failed with a reason). The game also supports an Exit action: when an Exit action is processed, the game sets an internal exit flag so
that shouldStop() becomes true and the main game loop terminates. In addition, shouldStop() must also return true
when the current GameState satisfies the win condition, i.e., GameState.isWin() returns true.
  2.3 Terminal UI: input, rendering, and main loop
  Terminal input commands are defined as follows (case-insensitive):
  - Player 0 uses W (up), A (left), S (down), D (right).
  - Player 1 uses K (up), H (left), J (down), L (right).
  - R triggers an Undo action with initiator = 0 (Player 0).
U triggers an Undo action with initiator = 1 (Player 1).
  - The command exit triggers an Exit action.
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```

```text
  - Any other input returns an InvalidInput action with initiator = -1 
  TerminalSokobanGame is the main runner extending AbstractSokobanGame, coordinating the terminal game loop. It restricts the terminal interface to a maximum of two players: when
  setState(GameState) is called, if the state contains more than two players, it throws IllegalArgumentException.
  TerminalSokobanGame.run() renders the initial board state before entering the loop, then repeatedly:
  1. fetches one action from TerminalInputEngine,
  2. processes it via processAction,
  3. prints a message through TerminalRenderingEngine.message(...),
  4. renders the updated state.
  During the game loop, the undo quota may be consulted (e.g., via GameState.getUndoQuota()).
  TerminalRenderingEngine is responsible for rendering the game grid to an output stream. TerminalRenderingEngine.message(String) prints the given content followed by a newline.
  2.4 Undo and win condition
  The game provides an Undo mechanism: transitions are accumulated during moves, and a checkpoint is recorded when a box is successfully pushed; checkpoints are stored in a history stack in
  GameState. When an Undo action is executed, the game reverts using the transition/checkpoint history. Undo transitions must be applied atomically to preserve the correct final state of all
  entities. undoQuota uses 0 as not allowed and -1 as unlimited, and finite quota is consumed only when there is a checkpoint in history to undo.
  A game is won (GameState.isWin) when every destination position in the map is currently occupied by a Box.
  ---
  3. External Utilities and Known Information
  SokobanGameFactory & Sokoban: The entry points that load map files, parse the board, and initialize the game engines.
  StringResources: A utility class centralizing all display messages and prompts (e.g., WIN_MESSAGE, INVALID_INPUT_MESSAGE, UNDO_QUOTA_TEMPLATE).

  ---
```
